summary: Two generations of NASA satellites watch the same fires and disagree: VIIRS (since 2012) reports two to three times more fire than MODIS (since 2000) for the same burning. Joined as they are, the records say the world burns 2.3× more than in the 2000s, when it actually burns less. Dala Fire puts the record on one scale: every country by month for 2001–2025, and one country, Kazakhstan, day by day from 2000 to yesterday. One factor per 3° tile, fitted on days when both sensors saw the same ground, turns MODIS counts into VIIRS-scale counts. We tested it instead of assuming it: leaving each year out, world totals miss by 0.9% (naive splice: 63.9%) and Kazakhstan's by 3.0% (50.8%). An independent NASA product agrees: burned area in Kazakhstan fell 3.22×, our record 3.17×, the naive splice only 1.37×. The result is a free web app with no login: pick any country or draw any area and see a burning calendar on one scale. For Kazakhstan it also tells whether this month is unusual, which regions burn above normal, and when the critical weeks come. It updates itself from NASA FIRMS every three hours.
details:
What Dala Fire Does

Dala Fire is an end-to-end harmonization pipeline and web app for NASA active-fire data. It ingests the MODIS (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21) hot-spot archives from NASA FIRMS, removes the break between the two sensor generations, and serves one consistent fire record: every country by month for 2001–2025, and Kazakhstan day by day from November 2000 to yesterday. A user picks a country or region, draws an area or uploads a polygon, and gets a burning calendar, a verdict on whether the current month is unusual, the critical weeks of the fire season, an accuracy check for that exact area, and CSV/PNG downloads. The record updates itself from FIRMS every three hours.

Why it is needed:

VIIRS (375 m) reports two to three times more fire than MODIS (1 km) for the same burning. Joined as they are, the records say the world burns 2.3× more than in 2003–2007. On one scale it burns about 14% less.

How It Works: Key Technical Steps

  1. Cleaning. MODIS detections with confidence ≥ 30; VIIRS with nominal or high confidence; vegetation fires only (FIRMS type 0).
  2. Static-source mask. Gas flares, industry and volcanoes are removed: any 0.01° cell with repeated detections of type 2 or 3 is masked together with its eight neighbours. Without the mask the tile error rises from 7.6% to 8.8%.
  3. Fire cell-days, the unit of the whole record. A fire cell-day is a 0.01° cell (~1 km) with at least one clean detection on a day. Counting cells instead of pixels removes most of the resolution difference before any correction: many 375 m VIIRS pixels from one fire fall into one cell. The factor depends on this choice (1.70 at 0.02°, 2.76 at 0.005°), so it is fixed and documented.
  4. Outage detection. A day when a satellite delivered nothing looks like a day without fire. A satellite-day is flagged as missing when it has zero detections or less than 25% of its 31-day running median, and cross-checked with the FIRMS missing-data list: 127 of its 178 days were already found by our rule, 13 were added. Missing days are shown as "no data", never as zero. Kazakhstan has 36 outage runs in 26 years.
  5. Harmonization to the VIIRS Suomi NPP scale. For every 3° tile:

    k_tile = (ΣV + Λ·k₀) / (ΣM + Λ)

    Where ΣV and ΣM are the VIIRS and MODIS fire cell-days of the tile on calibration days, k₀ is the factor of the whole area, and Λ = 200 shrinks tiles with little fire toward k₀. Calibration days are the 3,619 days of 20 Jan 2012 – 31 Dec 2021 on which Terra, Aqua and Suomi NPP all delivered data.
    • Kazakhstan: k₀ = 2.005; 58 tiles from 1.61 to 3.40.
    • World: k₀ = 2.753; 2,643 tiles, 10th–90th percentile 2.0–4.11.
    • Days with only one MODIS satellite use bridge factors (Kazakhstan: Terra 1.955, Aqua 1.860).
    • NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 are tied to Suomi NPP (0.998 and 1.035), so the record continued unchanged when Suomi NPP stopped on 2 November 2026.
  6. Source priority per day: Suomi NPP → NOAA-20 → NOAA-21 → both MODIS → one MODIS → no data. After 2012 the record is VIIRS itself; before 2012 it is MODIS × k_tile, flagged as modelled and shown with an uncertainty band.
  7. Additive model. The value of any area is the sum of its cells, so a region, a drawn polygon and the whole country are always consistent with each other.
  8. Delivery. 1.8 million cell-day rows in a 7 MB Parquet file; the browser aggregates any area in about 35 ms. No server and no API key in the browser.

Validation: Leave-One-Year-Out

Each year of 2012–2021 is predicted from MODIS with factors fitted on the other nine years, then compared with what Suomi NPP actually saw. Median absolute error of yearly totals:

Kazakhstan

  • Naive splice: country 50.8%, 3° tile 51.1%
  • One national factor: country 2.9%, tile 10.6% (90th percentile 25.3%)
  • Dala Fire, 3° tiles: country 3.0%, tile 7.6% (90th percentile 20.6%)

World (548 million detections, nothing retuned)

  • Naive splice: world 63.9%, tile 63.2%
  • One global factor: world 0.9%, tile 27.2%
  • Dala Fire, 3° tiles: world 0.9%, tile 9.0% (90th percentile 31.6%)
  • Nine world regions: 1.0% (southern Africa) to 3.8% (South Asia), bias at most 1.9%

Further tests

  • Backcast: factors fitted only on 2014–2021 predict 2012 and 2013 within +3.2% and −6.3% (world: +4.2% and +0.9%).
  • Stability: fitted on each calibration year separately, the VIIRS/MODIS ratio stays between 1.95 and 2.13 while yearly fire differed 4.3×. This is why one set of factors can be carried back to the fiery 2000s.
  • Model choice fixed in advance: a factor per tile and calendar month improved the world tile error by exactly 0.5 points; our rule required more than 0.5, so the simpler model is used.

Case Study 1: The 2012 Seam

2011 is the last MODIS-only year, 2012 the first VIIRS year.

  • Kazakhstan: naive splice ×4.53, MODIS alone (which flew both years) ×2.31, Dala Fire ×2.28.
  • World: naive splice ×2.58, MODIS alone ×1.04, Dala Fire ×1.01. The harmonized record moves like the one sensor that saw both years.

Case Study 2: Independent Check Against Burned Area

MODIS burned area (MCD64, Collection 6.1) maps burn scars from surface reflectance, not from heat, and has no 2012 seam. Nothing from it was used to fit the method.

  • Kazakhstan, 2001–2005 → 2019–2023: burned area fell 3.22×, Dala Fire 3.17×, naive splice 1.37×.
  • Fire cell-days per km² burned across 2012: Dala Fire 1.03 (level), naive splice 2.10 (doubles).
  • World: correlation of yearly totals with burned area is 0.86 for Dala Fire and −0.68 for the naive splice, which runs against reality.
  • 28 areas tested (Kazakhstan, 17 regions, world, 9 world regions): in 27 the harmonized decline is closer to burned area than the naive one.

Case Study 3: One Day in Kostanay

On 3 September 2022 Kostanay Region registered 508 fire cell-days, 60% of that month's burning in a single day. A monthly product hides this. The app lists the ten biggest fire days of any area and maps each one. On 1–14 November 2026 the same region burned 184 fire cell-days against a median of 11 for those days in 2016–2025, and the app flags it "unusually high".

Robustness: 12 Variants

One choice changed at a time, everything rerun: no confidence filter, stricter MODIS confidence, mask without dilation or removed, 0.005° or 0.02° cells, 2° or 5° tiles, shrinkage Λ from 0 to 1000, separate day and night factors.

  • Country error stays between 2.1% and 3.9% (naive: 50.8%).
  • The decline since the 2000s stays between 4.9× and 5.3×.
  • Separate day/night factors made every measure worse (3.6% and 8.7%), so they are not used.
  • No variant is best on every measure: the method was not tuned to its own test.

Anomalies and Critical Periods

  • "Is this month unusual?" The latest days are compared with the same calendar days of the last 10 years (switchable to all years since 2001). Levels by percentile: above 90 unusually high, 66–90 above normal, 33–66 near normal, 10–33 below normal, under 10 unusually low. A reference year counts only if at least 80% of its days have satellite data.
  • Why 10 years by default: fire in Kazakhstan fell 5.4× since the 2000s, so against 2001 almost every recent month would look "low".
  • Critical periods: the fewest weeks of the year that hold 75% of the usual burning.
  • Uncertainty: every modelled value carries an 80% band from the validation. For 1,000–3,000 fire cell-days the band is 0.82–1.13 of the estimate; for 3–10 it is 0.14–2.2, and the app marks such values as indicative.

Automatic Updates

Every three hours a GitHub Actions job requests near-real-time detections from the FIRMS API, applies the same cleaning, mask, grid and factors, adds each complete UTC day and redeploys the site. Run on the pipeline's own input, the updater reproduces the pipeline's output exactly (1,836,281 rows, no difference). The API key lives in a repository secret, never in code, logs or the browser.

What the Record Shows

  • World: less fire now than in 2003–2007, not 2.3× more.
  • Kazakhstan: fire fell 5.4× from 2001–2005 to 2021–2025 (naive splice: 2.3×). MODIS alone, never rescaled, shows 5.0×; VIIRS alone shows 2.1× since 2012–2014. Autumn burning fell 10×, spring burning 3×.

BENEFITS AND GOALS

Dala Fire gives an immediate, practical answer to "is this fire season unusual?" on a baseline that is not broken in 2012.

  • Emergency services see which regions burn above normal right now and what the next four weeks usually bring.
  • Farmers and land managers see when their region burns and how the season has shifted over 25 years.
  • Scientists and students get a reproducible, documented fire series for any country, with its uncertainty, instead of a hand-made splice.
  • Because every script is open and the method was tested on the whole planet without retuning, any country can be given the same day-by-day depth as Kazakhstan.

Long-term goal: a trusted long fire record that outlives MODIS and continues on the VIIRS satellites, so that early warning, land management and climate studies all read the same numbers. The project supports UN Sustainable Development Goals 13 (Climate Action) and 15 (Life on Land).

Team Thermal Fusion: Zhoshy Khalelov (captain) and Zhangir Abay.

Honest Limits

  • Region check: in 16 regions of Kazakhstan MODIS × factors stays within 2.2–7.6% of VIIRS. In Mangystau (oil and gas fields) and Shymkent the error is 71% and 65%: fire there is rare and comes from small steady heat sources that MODIS misses. The app warns the user in such areas.
  • Applied after 2021, MODIS-based estimates fall up to 9.5% short by 2025, consistent with the drifting orbits of Terra and Aqua. The record is unaffected, because after 2012 it uses VIIRS directly.
  • Burned area partly uses MODIS detections, so before 2012 that check is not fully independent. One region, Kyzylorda, disagrees with it.
  • In the world layer a tenth of tiles err by more than 30% in a single year. It is monthly and ends in 2025.
  • These are satellite hot spots, not registered fire incidents.

Roadmap

  • Days and weeks for the whole world from near-real-time data.
  • Alerts when a region moves above its normal range.
  • Kazakh and Russian interfaces.
  • Land-cover-specific factors (cropland, steppe, forest) and a correction for MODIS orbit drift.

🛠️ Tools

Python (pandas, NumPy, PyArrow, SciPy, Shapely, Matplotlib) · TypeScript, React, Vite, MapLibre GL, hyparquet · GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages. All code is open: https://github.com/zhxshy/dala-fire

An AI assistant (Claude) helped draft code, analysis and text. We ran every script on the full data and checked the numbers; this is stated in the README, on the Methods page and in each script's header.
